name: Ebira

summary.text: The Ebira live south-west of the Niger and Benue confluence, mainly in central Kogi State, where Okene has long been their centre. Ebira is spoken by about 2 million people. The Ebira Tao live around Okene; the Ebira Koto (Egbura) at Koton Karfe, Abaji and Toto; and a related people, the Etuno, at Igarra in Edo State.

areas.note: Koton Karfe, the headquarters, is "predominantly inhabited by the Egbura Kotos". Other peoples live in the LGA too.
Shared with Igala and Bassa communities. The Eganyi, an Ebira people, live here.
Toto is mainly Bassa and Egbura (Ebira).
The Egbura are among the indigenous peoples of Abaji, with the Bassa, Gbagyi and Ganagana.
Wikipedia lists Ogori/Magongo among the Ebira Tao LGAs, but the Ogori and Magongo are peoples with their own language; how many Ebira live here needs checking.
The Ebira Koto are the third of Bassa LGA’s three main peoples.

communities.name: Igarra (Etuno)
communities.note: The people of Igarra speak Etuno, which Glottolog counts as the Igara dialect of Ebira.

reviewNotes: The Ohinoyi’s seat (Okene) is not yet stated in a source, so the ruler is shown without a seat.
